theory.intro: A **conversion graph** is a straight line used to change one unit into another. For the direct variation conversions studied here, the line passes through the origin and its gradient is the conversion factor.
facts: The conversion factor is $k = \dfrac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}$. It gives the number of vertical-axis units per horizontal-axis unit.
Use $y = kx$ to convert from $x$ to $y$. To convert back, divide the known $y$ value by $k$.

foundation.solution_text:
$m = \dfrac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}$
$= \dfrac{72 - 0}{60 - 0}$
$= 1.2$
$y = 1.2x$
The exchange rate is $1.2$ SGD per AUD.

Graph $A$ shows direct proportion: its line passes through the origin, so $0$ L corresponds to $0$ gallons.
Graph $B$ does **not**: its line crosses the vertical axis at $32$, so $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ corresponds to $32^{\circ}\text{F}$, not $0^{\circ}\text{F}$.

mastery.question_text:
A conversion graph between Australian dollars ($x$) and Canadian dollars ($y$) is a straight line through the origin.
One point on the line is $(140, 154)$.
Find the exchange rate, then convert $\$60$ AUD to CAD.
mastery.solution_text:
$m = \dfrac{154}{140}$
$= 1.1$
The exchange rate is $1.1$ CAD per AUD.
$60 \times 1.1$
$= 66$
$\$60$ AUD $= \$66$ CAD
